title: Cross-Service SLO Rollback Coordination Playbook & Initiative Tracker
creator: Connor Hayes
description: Create a canonical playbook and initiative-level tracker for coordinating cross-service rollbacks tied to SLO breaches and error-budget exhaustion. This ticket unites runbook actions, escalation steps, rollback gating criteria, and a living dependency map so Product, SRE, and Platform teams can: (1) quickly determine whether to throttle/rollback a rollout when error budgets across dependent services are burning, (2) execute safe rollbacks with pre-approved owners and rollback windows, and (3) track initiative-level mitigation work until SLOs recover.
acceptance_criteria: A single Confluence playbook exists that describes detection -> triage -> rollback -> verification steps and is linked from the Reliability Initiative Hub
An initiative tracker spreadsheet / dashboard is live showing active error-budget burn per service, owner, rollout id, and last rollback decision
Rollback gating thresholds are defined as machine-readable alerts (Grafana/Alertmanager) with clear runbook links and assigned oncall contacts
A cross-service dependency map is published and stored in the initiative tracker with service owners and fallback variants
Two tabletop exercises completed with SRE + Platform + affected PMs; lessons captured and follow-up tickets created
Automated post-rollback checks (sampling SLI runbook queries) validate SLO recovery within defined windows
implementation_notes: Use existing SLI queries from the SLO library as the baseline; capture 5m and 1h burn rates
Add a lightweight column to the initiative tracker for 'rollback-approved-variants' and 'rollback-preconditions'
Where feasible, wire alerts to an incident channel with a decision checklist (canary-cutoff, fallback-model-id, capacity-throttle)
Coordinate with ENG runtime team for an API hook that marks 'rollout-locked' for service deployments during active rollbacks
Plan two tabletop drills: one for cascading EKST/queue backlog scenarios and one for noisy-KV-cache regressions

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ambiguous ownership during simultaneous service SLO breaches can delay rollback -> Mitigation: pre-declare primary decision owner per initiative and maintain oncall contact list
Risk: Over-reactive rollbacks causing unnecessary user impact -> Mitigation: add staged gates (partial throttle -> canary rollback -> full rollback) with automated rollback simulation checks
Risk: Alert fatigue with too many thresholds -> Mitigation: combine signals into a weighted 'burn-score' and only page after crossing a sustained window
